extensions.note: Extracted from the ten painted product surfaces and verified by computed style in a browser. No tonal ramps are recorded: the project declares no tonal scale, and synthesising one would put colours in this file that no surface uses.

green.usage: fill only — primary button, walked progress node, live status disc. 1.69:1 on page and 1.52:1 on card, so never text and never an icon stroke.

on-green.usage: the only colour permitted on a green fill — 9.46:1. Never white (1.84:1).

green-wash.usage: the one green tint — selected tab, verified badge, milestone marks. Charcoal on it 14.75:1; 1.085:1 against the page, so it is a hue signal, not a luminance one.

page.usage: screen ground and every system bar, so chrome melts into the page.

card.usage: every card surface. 1.11:1 step on the page.

media.usage: media wells, muted chips, skeleton ground. 1.20:1 step on the page.

btn2.usage: secondary button, circular icon actions, skeleton bars, settled status disc.

inset.usage: derived color-mix(page 55%, card) — the From/To strip. 1.06:1 above the card.

ink.usage: titles, values, button labels, every icon glyph, the focus ring.

slate.usage: labels, dates, keys, body copy, unselected tabs, pending milestones.

line.usage: bar borders, row rules, the pending progress track. 1.21:1 on the card.

warn.usage: declared, drawn nowhere — 1.84:1 on the card, so it cannot carry a mark.

warn-ink.usage: 5.65:1 on its wash — the ETA-slipping mark.

warn-wash.usage: the well behind the late-notice glyph.

danger.usage: declared, drawn nowhere — reaches only 4.07:1 on the card.

danger-ink.usage: 5.49:1 on its wash — signal lost, upload missing.

danger-wash.usage: the well behind the error glyph.

trust-ink.usage: the ink of a credential the platform has CONFIRMED — the Insured badge label and its checkmark. 5.65:1 on its own wash, the family rung --warn-ink already stands at; 5.93:1 on the card. Added 2026-08-15 (rev 58). It speaks and it strokes, which the fill-only rule permits because that rule is --green s.

trust-wash.usage: the ground of the confirmed-credential chip. The system s first cool colour and the third semantic wash beside warn and danger — not a second accent. 1.05:1 on the card, and 1.03:1 against the --media chip beside it, which is why the checkmark and not the hue carries the state (WCAG 1.4.1).

narrative.overview: Extracted from the ten painted product surfaces and verified by computed style in a browser, 2026-08-01. Four painted surfaces on one warm ramp — page #F7F5F2, card #ECE9E4, media #E4E1DA, secondary button #D6D2C9 — with no white and no black anywhere in the palette. Two inks: #1A1A1A and #5A5751; every rendered string on all ten pages is one of the two. One accent, #9BCF4A, always a fill or a tint and never text or an icon stroke, measured at 4.43% / 5.09% / 4.71% of the frame on the three base screens. No card and no media surface casts a shadow; one shadow is spent in the whole system, under the green primary. 98 icons, all on a 24-grid at stroke-width 1.7. One font stack, ten type sizes, six radii plus circles. Zero text-contrast failures, the lowest pair being 4.77:1.
keyCharacteristics: Four painted surfaces, one warm ramp — no white and no black in the palette
Two inks: #1A1A1A and #5A5751, and nothing else on a product surface
One accent, fill only — 1.69:1 on the page and 1.52:1 on the card, so never text and never a stroke
Measured green budget: 4.43% / 5.09% / 4.71% of the frame, the CTA being 81-100% of it
Flat: no card, panel, well, map or photograph casts a shadow
One icon system: 98 SVGs, 24-grid, stroke-width 1.7, fill none, currentColor
One font stack declared once; ten type sizes, all in use
Six radii plus circles for objects, the 2 / 4 / 8 scale for internal details; leading is 1.4 by inheritance and overridden only where the box demands it

rules.name: The Fill-Only Rule
rules.body: Green is a fill, a tint, or a ring. It is never a text colour, never an icon stroke, and never a border on its own. Anything sitting on green or on the green tint is --ink.

rules.name: The Two-Ink Rule
rules.body: A string is --ink or --slate. There is no third text colour on a product surface, and no colour-coded text of any kind.

rules.name: The Wash-Carries-Ink Rule
rules.body: A semantic state is a pale wash with its own darkened ink on top. The saturated hue is declared for reference and drawn nowhere.

rules.name: The No-White-No-Black Rule
rules.body: The palette has no #FFFFFF and no #000000. Even the shadows are warm — every one is rgba(20, 18, 15, ...).

rules.name: The Ten-Sizes Rule
rules.body: On a product surface the ten sizes are the whole scale. A size that is none of them is a size nobody chose.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any figure a user compares or verifies — money, time, ETA, rating — carries font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Structure Rule
rules.body: The mono face labels structure, never content: zone annotations, FROM / TO / LOCATION, loading hints. No product string is set in mono.

rules.name: The Between-Beats-Within Rule
rules.body: Proximity groups in the right direction without a border or a shadow, but the rule holds per level, not as one number. Where the list IS the screen, the gap between two cards (28) is larger than any gap inside one (<=20). Where the list is one zone among several, the level above it takes over: main separates zones by 16, so the cards must close to 12 (.dr-list--snug) or they read as further apart than the zones themselves. 12 is still above the 4px rhythm inside a card, and the card's interior stays bounded by its drawn edge (--card on --page at 1.11:1 plus the 16px radius), not by whitespace it has to win.

rules.name: The Skeleton-Measures-The-Load Rule
rules.body: A loading block is the size of the thing it waits for. A skeleton is a claim about the loaded screen, so it expires when that screen changes treatment.

rules.name: The One-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Exactly one shadow is spent, and it is under the primary button. A card that casts no shadow at rest cannot grow one on hover.

rules.name: The Tone-Step Rule
rules.body: Separation between two surfaces is a warm tone step plus a radius, and the step is measured before it is used. A surface boundary is a decorative edge — not text (1.4.3), not a control or state indicator (1.4.11) — so no contrast minimum applies to it.

rules.name: The Closed-Ramp Rule
rules.body: Six radii and a circle for anything the eye reads as an object — a surface, a control, a well, a chip. Below that, an internal detail may take any radius on the 2 / 4 / 8 scale.

rules.name: The Cut-By-The-Parent Rule
rules.body: A full-bleed child is square and the parent's overflow:hidden gives it the corner. It never restates the parent's radius.

rules.name: The One-Component-One-Value Rule
rules.body: The same component drawn on two screens carries the same numbers. The tracking ETA panel and the delivery details panel are one component; the order card's node and the tracking timeline's node are one node.

rules.name: The Built-Not-Dimmed Rule
rules.body: A disabled or inactive control is built from its own colour pair. Blanket opacity is never the mechanism — it produces a ratio nobody measured.

rules.name: The Shape-And-Behaviour Rule
rules.body: Two states never differ by colour alone. A dot pings and a check sits; a clock is not a check; each keeps a text accessible name.

dos: Do spend green as a fill and put --ink on it — 9.46:1 on the fill, 14.75:1 on the tint.
Do keep solid green at or under ~5% of the frame, with the primary CTA as most of it.
Do separate surfaces with a warm tone step and a radius, and measure the step before using it.
Do give a state two signals — a shape and an ink change, or a glyph and a title.
Do use min-height for anything that must stay a 44pt target.
Do size a skeleton block to the element it waits for, and re-measure it when that element changes treatment.
Do let a cutout sit straight on the card and a photograph cover its whole surface.
Do write the contrast ratio next to any new pair, before it ships.
Do check every decision against HIG and WCAG 2.1 AA, and report a mismatch with the exact value, the named criterion and the number.
donts: Don't set text or an icon stroke in --green — 1.69:1 on the page, 1.52:1 on the card.
Don't introduce a darkened green as an ink. --green-ink #3F5B18 was deleted for exactly this reason: a darkened accent is still the accent used as text.
Don't add a shadow to a card, a panel, a well, a map or a photograph. One shadow exists and it is under the primary button.
Don't spend green inside card UI — the direction chip, the route strip and card actions are neutral.
Don't give a surface, control, well or chip a radius outside the six, and don't restate a parent's radius on a full-bleed child. Internal details may use the 2 / 4 / 8 scale.
Don't dim a control with blanket opacity — build the disabled state from its own pair.
Don't draw the raw semantic hue. A state is a wash carrying its own ink.
Don't let a state be carried by colour alone.
Don't upscale a cutout, add a ground under one in the product, or mix a grid of drones into a product screen.
Don't compensate an icon's stroke-width to hold a constant rendered weight — declare 1.7 on the 24-grid and change the size instead.
